:::

## Xiàhóu Shàng {.unnumbered #xiahoushang}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Xiàhóu Shàng appellation Bórén was [Xiàhóu] Yuān's cousin's son. Emperor Wén was close friends with him. <a href="#annotation-37" id="source-37">[37]</a> When Tàizǔ settled Jì Province, [Xiàhóu] Shàng became Army Major, commanded cavalry following on campaigns, later became Five Offices General's Literary Scholar. When Wèi state was first established, promoted to Yellow Gate Attendant Cadet. Dài prefecture's Hú rebelled, sent the Marquess of Yānlíng [Cáo] Zhāng to campaign and suppress them, with [Xiàhóu] Shàng as Advisor to [Cáo] Zhāng's military affairs, settled Dài territory, returned. Tàizǔ passed away at Luòyáng, [Xiàhúo] Shàng Held Stave to serve the catalpa coffin in returning to Yè. Altogether noted former achievements, enfeoffed Marquess of Pínglíng precinct, appointed Cavalier Regular Attendant, promoted to Central Manager of the Army. When Emperor Wén ascended the throne, further enfeoffed as Marquess of Pínglíng village, promoted to Campaigning South General, designate Jīng Province Inspector, Lent Stave as Overall Supervisor of the south's various military affairs. [Xiàhóu] Shàng memorialized: "Liú Bèi's separate army is at Shàngyōng, the mountain roads rugged and difficult, they do not expect us, if we use surprise troops secretly traveling, setting out where they do not expect, then it is a situation for an independent success." Therefore organized the various armies and struck and defeated Shàngyōng, pacified three prefectures and nine counties, promoted to Campaigning South General-in-Chief. Although Sūn Quán declared himself vassal, [Xiàhóu] Shàng increasingly prepared equipment for attacking and suppressing, [Sūn] Quán later indeed had duplicitous heart. Huángchū Third Year [222], the Chariot Carriage visited Wǎn, sent [Xiàhóu] Shàng to lead the various armies with Cáo Zhēn to together besiege Jiānglíng. [Sūn] Quán's officer Zhūgě Jǐn with [Xiàhóu] Shàng's army faced on the Jiāng, [Zhūgě] Jǐn crossed to enter an islet in the Jiāng, and divided a navy in the Jiāng. [Xiàhóu] Shàng in the night prepared main oiled ships,^[According to Hú Sānxǐng's commentary in the Zīzhì Tōngjiàn, oiled ships were boats coated with a layer of oil to repel water.] commanded infantry and cavalry of over ten thousand men, to the downstream secretly crossed, attacked [Zhūgě] Jǐn's various armies, pinsered the Jiāng and burned their boats, water and land all attacking, defeated them. The city was not yet taken, it happened that a great epidemic, Edict ordered [Xiàhóu] Shàng to withdraw the various armies and return. Increased fief by six hundred households, adding with the previous to one thousand nine hundred households, Lent Battle-Ax, advanced to Governor. Jīng Province was ravaged and desolate, outside bordered Mán-Yí, and with Wú blocking the Hàn river as a border, of the old population many resided south of the Jiāng. [Xiàhóu] Shàng from Shàngyōng connected roads, west traveling over seven hundred lǐ, of the mountain peoples and Mán-Yí many submitted, within five to six years the surrendered and attached were several thosuand families. Fifth Year [224], relocated enfeoffment to Marquess of Chānglíng village. [Xiàhóu] Shàng had a beloved concubine favored with visits, favor taken away from the primary wife. The primary wife was the Cáo clan's daughter, therefore Emperor Wén sent someone to strangle and kill her. [Xiàhóu] Shàng was sorrowful and emotional, fell ill and became dazed. After already burying the concubine, he could not bear his longing to see her, and again excavated her to see her. Emperor Wén heard and was enraged at him, and said: "Dù Xí's disparagement of [Xiàhóu] Shàng had a good reason." However as he was an old minster, the grace and favor did not decline. Sixth Year [225], [Xiàhóu] Shàng's illness was critical, reeturned to the capital city, the Emperor repeatedly visited him, held his hand and shed tears. [Xiàhóu] Shàng died, posthumous name called Dào-hóu.^[Though this biography dates Xiàhóu Shàng's illness as starting in the Sixth Year, the Treatises on Astronomy in Jìn shū record that Xiàhóu Shàng did not actually die until the Fourth Moon of the Seventh Year (226).] <a href="#annotation-38" id="source-38">[38]</a> His son [Xiàhóu] Xuán succeeded. Also divided from [Xiàhóu] Shàng households of three hundred to bestow on [Xiàhóu] Shàng's younger brother's son [Xiàhóu] Fèng noble title as Marquess Within the Passes.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
夏侯尚字伯仁，淵從子也。文帝與之親友。〔一〕太祖定冀州，尚為軍司馬，將騎從征伐，後為五官將文學。魏國初建，遷黃門侍郎。代郡胡叛，遣鄢陵侯彰征討之，以尚參彰軍事，定代地，還。太祖崩于洛陽，尚持節，奉梓宮還鄴。并錄前功，封平陵亭侯，拜散騎常侍，遷中領軍。文帝踐阼，更封平陵鄉侯，遷征南將軍，領荊州刺史，假節都督南方諸軍事。尚奏：「劉備別軍在上庸，山道險難，彼不我虞，若以奇兵潛行，出其不意，則獨克之勢也。」遂勒諸軍擊破上庸，平三郡九縣，遷征南大將軍。孫權雖稱藩，尚益脩攻討之備，權後果有貳心。黃初三年，車駕幸宛，使尚率諸軍與曹真共圍江陵。權將諸葛瑾與尚軍對江，瑾渡入江中渚，而分水軍于江中。尚夜多持油船，將步騎萬餘人，於下流潛渡，攻瑾諸軍，夾江燒其舟船，水陸並攻，破之。城未拔，會大疫，詔敕尚引諸軍還。益封六百戶，并前千九百戶，假鉞，進為牧。荊州殘荒，外接蠻夷，而與吳阻漢水為境，舊民多居江南。尚自上庸通道，西行七百餘里，山民蠻夷多服從者，五六年間，降附數千家。五年，徙封昌陵鄉侯。尚有愛妾嬖幸，寵奪適室；適室，曹氏女也，故文帝遣人絞殺之。尚悲感，發病恍惚，既葬埋妾，不勝思見，復出視之。文帝聞而恚之曰：「杜襲之輕薄尚，良有以也。」然以舊臣，恩寵不衰。六年，尚疾篤，還京都，帝數臨幸，執手涕泣。尚薨，諡曰悼侯。〔二〕子玄嗣。又分尚戶三百，賜尚弟子奉爵關內侯。
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-37" id="annotation-37">[37]</a> Wèi shū states: [Xiàhóu] Shàng had strategic planning and tactical wisdom, Emperor Wén valued him, and they became friends in plain clothes.^[Friends in plain clothes (bùyī zhī jiāo) refers to a friendship formed before achieving high rank and status.]
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　魏書曰：尚有籌畫智略，文帝器之，與為布衣之交。
:::
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-38" id="annotation-38">[38]</a> Wèi shū records the Edict stating: "[Xiàhóu] Shàng from youth attended and followed, thorough in sincerity and exhaustive in integrity, though he was said to be of a different surname, he was like my bone and flesh,^[Bone and flesh (gǔ ròu) is an idiom for biological relation, and can perhaps be considered an equivalent for the English "flesh and blood."] therefore in entering he was my belly and heart, in exiting he was my claws and teeth. His tactical wisdom was deep and quick, his planning surpassed others, by misfortune he early died, such is fate, what can be done? Posthumously bequeath the Campaigning South General-in-Chief's and Marquess of Chānglíng's seals and ribbons."
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔二〕　魏書載詔曰：「尚自少侍從，盡誠竭節，雖云異姓，其猶骨肉，是以入為腹心，出當爪牙。智略深敏，謀謨過人，不幸早殞，命也奈何！贈征南大將軍、昌陵侯印綬。」
:::

### Xiàhóu Xuán {.unnumbered #xiahouxuan}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
[Xiàhóu] Xuán appellation Tàichū. In youth he was famed, on capping^[Capping (ruò guàn) referred to the ceremony marking the transition to adulthood, when a man began wearing an adult headdress and hat. The ceremony was usually performed at age twenty in traditional reckoning.] became Cavalier Yellow Gate Attendant Cadet. Once in advancing for a meeting, he was with the Imperial Empress's younger brother Máo Zēng seated together. [Xiàhóu] Xuán was shamed by this, displeasuring showing in his expression. Emperor Míng resented this, demoted him to Feather Forest Overseer. At Zhèngshǐ's beginning, Cáo Shuǎng assisted in government. [Xiàhóu] Xuán was [Cáo] Shuǎng's father's sister's son. Gradually promoted to Cavalier Regular Attendant, Central Protector of the Army. <a href="#annotation-39" id="source-39">[39]</a>
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
玄字太初。少知名，弱冠為散騎黃門侍郎。嘗進見，與皇后弟毛曾並坐，玄恥之，不悅形之於色。明帝恨之，左遷為羽林監。正始初，曹爽輔政。玄，爽之姑子也。累遷散騎常侍、中護軍。〔一〕
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-39" id="annotation-39">[39]</a> Shìyǔ states: [Xiàhóu] Xuán was famous for understanding men, became Central Protector of the Army, selecting and employing military offices, the advisors and guards and Ivory Gates,^[Ivory Gates (yámén) referred to the office tents of Generals, which were marked by ivory-tipped banners to form gates.] none were not outstanding talents, many became Governors of provinces and managers of prefectures. His established laws and bequeathed instructions to the present all were models for posterity.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　世語曰：玄世名知人，為中護軍，拔用武官，參戟牙門，無非俊傑，多牧州典郡。立法垂教，于今皆為後式。
:::
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Grand Tutor Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng asked him about the time's affairs, [Xiàhóu] Xuán commented believing: "The appointment of talents and employment of people, is the handle of the state. Therefore, evaluations and selections being concentrated at the Terrace Pavillion is the responsibility of the above; filial conduct maintained in the village alleys, merits and drawbacks assigned by village peoples, is the ordering of the below. The desire to purify instruction and investigate selections, is in making clear the responsibility and ordering, not allowing them to encroach on one another, and nothing more. Why is this? If the above overstep their responsibility, then one fears that their origins will not be from the roots, and so open the road to grasping at power and chasing influence. If the below exceed their ordering, then one fears that celestial titles will be connected with the exterior, and so the gates to critical power will be many. Celestial titles connecting with the below, is for common people to discuss the handles (of power). Critical power having many gates, is the origin of disorder and chaos. Since the coming of provincial and prefectural Central Rectifiers ranking and grading the appointments of talents, it has been for many years, remaining disordered, never hearing of organization, how is this not due to responsibility and ordering becoming intermingled, each losing their essentials? If it is ordered that Central Rectifiers only examine conduct by class of peers, the standard of conduct for a class of peers being matched, this can be appointed. Why is this? If filial conduct is proven in the family gates, how can they not be loyal and scrupulous in their appointments? If benevolence and forbearance is praised in the nine clans, how can they not be understanding in enacting government? If righteous decisiceness is enacted in the home community, how can they not be able to bear tasks and assignments? These three categories, selected by the Central Rectifiers, even if they do not place them in appointed office, the fitness for appointment can be known. Conduct has large and small, comparisons have high and low, then the categories of appointments, also naturally become clearly differentiated. Why must one have the Central Rectifiers interfere in the mechanisms of evaluations and selections at the below, and so have those grasping the mechanisms and handles have to delegate authority from above, above and below infringing on one another, and so creating disordered intermingling? Moreover the Terrace Pavillions oversee the below, examining achievements and inspecting wrongs, the associates of the numerous duties, each have their office chiefs, dawn to dusk examining one another, nothing investigates as thoroughly as this. The discussions of the village alleys, are determined by opinions, and so if it causes skilled administrators to lose positions, everyone becomes agitated and alarmed. The desire for social customs to be purified and tranquil, how could it be obtained? The Celestial Terrace hangs far away, cut off from the opinions of the masses. Those able to arrive, further are close nearby, who would not craft embellishments to obtain what they seek? Once there is a road to what they seek, then those that cultivated themselves in their family gates, already cannot compare to those who advanced themselves in their local communities, and those that advanced themselves in their local communities, already cannot compare to those that themselves sought it from the provincial authorities. If one opens that road, and yet worries that the embellishment of the true will depart from the roots, even if one further strictly reproached the Central Rectifiers, disciplining them with punishments, yet it would be without benefit. How would it compare to having each command their responsibility, the office chiefs then would each by the capability or inability of their associates proffer them to the Terrace Pavillions, the Terrace Pavillions then would act in accordance to the rankings of the capability or inability of the office chiefs, supplemented with the gradings of virtue and conduct in local communities, assessed in comparison to peers, without allowing partiality or bias. Central Rectifiers then would only examine the conduct and legacies, differentiating the high and low, judging and determining categories, without allowing promotion or demotion. The Terrace Pavillions would control it, in accordance with their selections. If there are mistakes, then the responsibility naturally is on the relevant managers. The rankings by the office chiefs, the categorizations by Central Rectifiers, compare and in accordance to established grading then employ them, and if they are not suitable, the responsibility is on the exterior. That being the case, interior and exterior consult with one another, successes and failures have their attributions, each exposing and inspecting one another, who would be able to embellish one another? Then the people's hearts are settled and affairs are managed and completed, and perhaps we may tranquilize social custom and examine the appointment of talents."

He also believed: "The ancients established offices in order to aid and nurture the various living, preside and administer the people. Therefore they appointed lords and chiefs to manage and herd them. The principle of managing and herding, is a wish to unify and concentrate. If unified then office responsibilities are settled and so above and below are secure. If concentrated then duties are performed and so affairs are not cumbersome. When affairs are simple and duties performed, a case of above and below both secure and yet not governed, has never been. The Former Kings established myriad states, although the details cannot be recovered and thoroughly investigated, however they divided borders and drew boundaries, each guarding their territory, then this was not a system of overlapping restraints. Down to investigate the orderings of the Five Ranks of Yīn and Zhōu, it only had the differentiation of small and large and noble and lowly, and also had no lords and officials and servants and people yet having two chains of command restraining one another. If the official chain of command is not unified, then duties are not performed. If duties are not performed, then how can matters be kept simple? If matters are not simple, then how can the people be kept tranquil? If the people are not tranquil, then wrongdoing and evil together arise, and so treachery and fraud grow and expand. The Former Kings understood it would be like this, and therefore concentrated the duties of management and unified the chain of command. Beginning from Qín's era, they did not take as teacher the sagely ways, used self-interest in managing duties, used treachery in treating subordinates. Fearing the governing officials would not perform, they established overseers to supervise them, and fearing the overseers would tolerate wrongdoing, they established inspectors to investigate them. Governors and supervisors entangled one another, overseers and inspectors managed one another, the people harbored divergent hearts, above and below separated in functions. Hàn continued these threads, none able to rectify and reform it. In the expansion of the Wèi House, the days did not have the leisure to attend to it. The institutions of the Five Ranks, although difficult to suddenly restore, can be roughly established in ceremony and standards in order to unify the government system. The present chief clerks all govern the clerks and people, with another layer of the prefecture Administrators, added again with the Inspectors. If the jurisdiction of the prefecture is only in overall scope, then it is the same as with the province, and no reason for a duplication. It is appropriate to abolish the prefecture Administrator, and only appoint Inspectors. If the Inspector duty is kept then supervision is not abandoned. The prefectural clerks numbering in the tens of thousands will return to personally farming, thus reducing complexity and costs, increasing wealth and growing grain. This is first. The talents of large counties all can be prefecture administrators. Disputes over right or wrong always create differing opinions. To comply then is peace, to maintain oneself then is conflict. The beauty of harmonious stew is in uniting the different, the advantage of above and below is in the ability to complement one another. Compliance for peace, this is the zither and zithern playing one note.^[The qín and sè are two ancient stringed instruments, celebrated for being able to harmonize with one another. To have the two play the same note is a waste of their ability to harmonize different notes.] To sweep away and eliminate this, then offices are reduced and matters are simplified. This is second. Also the clerks of administering prefectures, their duty is to oversee the various counties, they strive to protect their faction and kin, local connections and old associates, if any do not submit, then they take advantage of public affairs to harass and obstruct. The destitution and distress of the people arises from this. If they were all merged and combined, then the source of the chaos would naturally be blocked. This is third. Now having inherited decline and damage, the people are diminished and depleted, worthy talents are rare and few, those appointed to affairs are scarce. The good clerks of prefectures and counties, generally are not only one, the prefectures receive what counties complete, thus the demanding work is below, but in the selecting above of clerks, the prefectures are the first supplied, this is to make the clerks closest to the people to be concentrated with the lowest caliber. The clerks determine the lives of the people, but yet are often stubborn and crude. Now if merging them, more clerks selected as pure and good will fill these duties, great cultivation will spread and flow, the people will attain peace. This is fourth. Systemize by having counties of ten thousand households be called as prefecture Administrators, five thousand and above called as Commandants, thousand households and below, Magistrates and Chiefs as before. From Chief and above, examine and test for promotion and employment, transfer and by ability rise, and those they govern will also increase, this is an ordering for advancing talent and rewarding achievement. If the core system is unified and settled, then appointment of talents has sequencing, and the achievements of governing will be uniform and clear. This is fifth. If the prefecture Administrators are abolished, the counties all directly connected, matters are not obstructed and partitioned, offices are without delay, and although the airs of the Three Dynasties cannot yet be guaranteed, the transformation of simplicity and unity, perhaps can be delivered. Conveniencing the people and reducing costs is in this."

He also believed: "Refinement and substance alternate in use, like the four seasons in succession rise. A King that embodies Heaven and orders people, must in response to detriments then relieve and resolve them, in seasons of excessive substance then refine them with rituals, in seasons of extreme extravagance then rescue them with substance. Now in inheriting the end of the Hundred Kings, the lingering flows of Qín and Hàn, the worldy customs are excessively refined, it is appropriate to greatly reform them to change the people's expectations. In present laws and regulations, from Dukes and Ranked Marquesses on down and positions from General-in-Chief and above, all are able to wear damask brocade, patterned silks, delicate white silks, objects of gold and silver ornaments and engravings, from this on down, clothes of mixed colors are available through to the lowly people. Although above and below ranks and grades each show their differentiations, however the systems of the Court ministers already are able to compare to the Utmost Honored, the colors of dark and yellow are already available through to subordinates. A desire to have the market not sell flowery and gorgeous colors, merchants not trade difficult to obtain goods, crafters not make engraved objects, cannot be obtained. Therefore it is appropriate to greatly manage the roots, standardize and limit by ancient laws, by the appropriateness of refinement and substance take the middle standards, to be ritual norms. Chariot carriages and clothing insignia, all are to follow substance and simplicity, prohibit and eliminate the flowery and gorgeous matters of end point customs, cause the families of those serving at Court and the households of those with positions to no longer have ornaments of brocade and patterned silk, be without clothing of multiple colors, and objects of delicate intricacies. From the above on down, reach to differentiation of plainness and simplicity, to show the ranks and grades and nothing more, and not allow it to exceed one to two distinctions. As for bestowments for achievements and virtues, and what the Superior's grace specially applies, all are to be registered by relevant managers, and only afterward worn and used. The above influencing the below, is like the wind bending grass. If the teachings of plain simplicity rise in the current Court, then the heart of excessive extravagance will on its own vanish below."
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
太傅司馬宣王問以時事，玄議以為：「夫官才用人，國之柄也，故銓衡專於臺閣，上之分也，孝行存乎閭巷，優劣任之鄉人，下之敘也。夫欲清教審選，在明其分敘，不使相涉而已。何者？上過其分，則恐所由之不本，而干勢馳騖之路開；下踰其敘，則恐天爵之外通，而機權之門多矣。夫天爵下通，是庶人議柄也；機權多門，是紛亂之原也。自州郡中正品度官才之來，有年載矣，緬緬紛紛，未聞整齊，豈非分敘參錯，各失其要之所由哉！若令中正但考行倫輩，倫輩當行均，斯可官矣。何者？夫孝行著於家門，豈不忠恪於在官乎？仁恕稱於九族，豈不達於為政乎？義斷行於鄉黨，豈不堪於事任乎？三者之類，取於中正，雖不處其官名，斯任官可知矣。行有大小，比有高下，則所任之流，亦渙然明別矣。奚必使中正干銓衡之機於下，而執機柄者有所委仗於上，上下交侵，以生紛錯哉？且臺閣臨下，考功校否，眾職之屬，各有官長，旦夕相考，莫究於此；閭閻之議，以意裁處，而使匠宰失位，眾人驅駭，欲風俗清靜，其可得乎？天臺縣遠，眾所絕意。所得至者，更在側近，孰不脩飾以要所求？所求有路，則脩己家門者，已不如自達于鄉黨矣。自達鄉黨者，已不如自求之於州邦矣。苟開之有路，而患其飾真離本，雖復嚴責中正，督以刑罰，猶無益也。豈若使各帥其分，官長則各以其屬能否獻之臺閣，臺閣則據官長能否之第，參以鄉閭德行之次，擬其倫比，勿使偏頗。中正則唯考其行跡，別其高下，審定輩類，勿使升降。臺閣總之，如其所簡，或有參錯，則其責負自在有司。官長所第，中正輩擬，比隨次率而用之，如其不稱，責負在外。然則內外相參，得失有所，互相形檢，孰能相飾？斯則人心定而事理得，庶可以靜風俗而審官才矣。」又以為：「古之建官，所以濟育群生，統理民物也，故為之君長以司牧之。司牧之主，欲一而專，一則官任定而上下安，專則職業脩而事不煩。夫事簡業脩，上下相安而不治者，未之有也。先王建萬國，雖其詳未可得而究，然分疆畫界，各守土境，則非重累羈絆之體也。下考殷、周五等之敘，徒有小大貴賤之差，亦無君官臣民而有二統互相牽制者也。夫官統不一，則職業不脩；職業不脩，則事何得而簡？事之不簡，則民何得而靜？民之不靜，則邪惡並興，而姦偽滋長矣。先王達其如此，故專其職司而一其統業。始自秦世，不師聖道，私以御職，姦以待下；懼宰官之不脩，立監牧以董之，畏督監之容曲，設司察以糾之；宰牧相累，監察相司，人懷異心，上下殊務。漢承其緒，莫能匡改。魏室之隆，日不暇及，五等之典，雖難卒復，可麤立儀準以一治制。今之長吏，皆君吏民，橫重以郡守，累以刺史。若郡所攝，唯在大較，則與州同，無為再重。宜省郡守，但任刺史；刺史職存則監察不廢，郡吏萬數，還親農業，以省煩費，豐財殖穀，一也。大縣之才，皆堪郡守，是非之訟，每生意異，順從則安，直己則爭。夫和羹之美，在於合異，上下之益，在能相濟，順從乃安，此琴瑟一聲也，蕩而除之，則官省事簡，二也。又幹郡之吏，職監諸縣，營護黨親，鄉邑舊故，如有不副，而因公掣頓，民之困弊，咎生于此，若皆并合，則亂原自塞，三也。今承衰弊，民人彫莈，賢才鮮少，任事者寡，郡縣良吏，往往非一，郡受縣成，其劇在下，而吏之上選，郡當先足，此為親民之吏，專得底下，吏者民命，而常頑鄙，今如并之，吏多選清良者造職，大化宣流，民物獲寧，四也。制使萬戶之縣，名之郡守，五千以上，名之都尉，千戶以下，令長如故，自長以上，考課遷用，轉以能升，所牧亦增，此進才效功之敘也，若經制一定，則官才有次，治功齊明，五也。若省郡守，縣皆徑達，事不擁隔，官無留滯，三代之風，雖未可必，簡一之化，庶幾可致，便民省費，在於此矣。」又以為：「文質之更用，猶四時之迭興也，王者體天理物，必因弊而濟通之，時彌質則文之以禮，時泰侈則救之以質。今承百王之末，秦漢餘流，世俗彌文，宜大改之以易民望。今科制自公、列侯以下，位從大將軍以上，皆得服綾錦、羅綺、紈素、金銀飾鏤之物，自是以下，雜綵之服，通于賤人，雖上下等級，各示有差，然朝臣之制，已得侔至尊矣，玄黃之采，已得通於下矣。欲使市不鬻華麗之色，商不通難得之貨，工不作彫刻之物，不可得也。是故宜大理其本，準度古法，文質之宜，取其中則，以為禮度。車輿服章，皆從質樸，禁除末俗華麗之事，使幹朝之家，有位之室，不復有錦綺之飾，無兼采之服，纖巧之物，自上以下，至于樸素之差，示有等級而已，勿使過一二之覺。若夫功德之賜，上恩所特加，皆表之有司，然後服用之。夫上之化下，猶風之靡草。樸素之教興於本朝，則彌侈之心自消於下矣。」
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
[Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng's reply letter said: "Scrutinizing offices and selecting men, eliminating redundant offices, reforming clothing regulations, all are very good. Respecting local community root conduct, the Court examining matters, the main point is as you indicated. But in the interim's it all became successively maintained habits, in the end it cannot be reformed. In Qín's time there were no Inspectors, only having Prefecture Administrators and Chief Clerks. Although the Hàn House had Inspectors, they observed Six Statutes and nothing more, and therefore Inspectors were called as Transfer Chariots, their clerks were called Following Officials, their residences had no regular headquarters, their clerks did not become complete servants, only from then afterward they transformed further into official managers. In the past Jiǎ Yì also worried over clothing regulations, although Hàn Wén's personal clothing was coarse silk, yet he was not able to cause above and below to be as he wished. One fears that these three matters must wait for the worthy and capable and only afterward be resolved."

[Xiàhóu] Xuán also wrote letter that said: "Although Hàn Wén personally wore coarse silk, yet he did not reform and correct the law institutions, the interior and exterior had clothing of usurpative imitation, favored servants received bestowals without limits, by this observing him, it seems his direction was to establish a reputation for himself, it was not an intention to sincerely standardize and govern regulations. Now Your Excellency Marquess has been mandated by the world to be the highest minister, follows the footsteps of high antiquity, seeking to expand to utmost governance, restrict tips and correct the roots, if the regulations are settled at the top, then transformation spreads to the multitudes. When facing a time appropriate for reform, one should keep an eagerly diligent heart. On the day the order is issued, the answer of those below is like merely an echo following a sound. Yet you hold to excessive modesty, stating: 'Wait for the worthy and capable,' this is Yī and Zhōu not correcting the standards of Yīn and Jī.^[Yī Yǐn was a celebrated minsiter of the Yīn dynasty. Zhōu-gōng was a celebrated minister of the Zhōu dynasty. The ruling family of Zhōu had the surname Jī.] I humbly do not understand it."
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
宣王報書曰：「審官擇人，除重官，改服制，皆大善。禮鄉閭本行，朝廷考事，大指如所示。而中間一相承習，卒不能改。秦時無刺史，但有郡守長吏。漢家雖有刺史，奉六條而已，故刺史稱傳車，其吏言從事，居無常治，吏不成臣，其後轉更為官司耳。昔賈誼亦患服制，漢文雖身服弋綈，猶不能使上下如意。恐此三事，當待賢能然後了耳。」玄又書曰：「漢文雖身衣弋綈，而不革正法度，內外有僭擬之服，寵臣受無限之賜，由是觀之，似指立在身之名，非篤齊治制之意也。今公侯命世作宰，追蹤上古，將隆至治，抑末正本，若制定於上，則化行於眾矣。夫當宜改之時，留殷勤之心，令發之日，下之應也猶響尋聲耳，猶垂謙謙，曰『待賢能』，此伊周不正殷姬之典也。竊未喻焉。」
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Shortly after this, he became Campaigning West General, Lent Stave as Overall Supervisor of Yōng and Liáng Provinces' various military affairs. <a href="#annotation-40" id="source-40">[40]</a> With Cáo Shuǎng they together raised the Luò valley campaign, at the time people ridiculed him. When [Cáo] Shuǎng was executed, summoned [Xiàhóu] Xuán to be Minister Herald, in a few years transferred to Minister of Ceremonies. [Xiàhóu] Xuán, because of [Cáo] Shuǎng was restrained and dismissed, inside he was not content. Central Writers Director Lǐ Fēng although formerly had been by General-in-Chief Sīmǎ [Shī] Jǐng-wáng closely treated, however his private heart was with [Xiàhóu] Xuán, and therefore he joined the Imperial Empress's father the Radiant Grandee Zhāng Qī to plot a wish to have [Xiàhóu] Xuán assist the government. [Lǐ] Fēng already inside held the handles of power, his son was bestowed a princess, and also he and [Zhāng] Qī both were Féngyì men, therefore [Zhāng] Qī trusted him. [Lǐ] Fēng secretly ordered his younger brother the Yǎn Province Inspector [Lǐ] Yì to request to enter Court, wishing to have him lead troops to enter, and combine strength to rise up. It happened that [Lǐ] Yì's request to attend Court was not permitted. Jiāpíng Sixth Year Second Moon [254 Mar 6 - Apr 4], there was to be an appointment of a Noble Lady, [Lǐ] Fēng and the rest wished to take advantage of the Imperial oversight of the pavillions, the various gates having ramp troops,^[This refers to the Emperor personally attending the ceremony, and soldiers posted at the ramp steps at the various gates of the Palace complex.] to execute the General-in-Chief, with [Xiàhóu] Xuán succeeding him, and with [Zhāng] Qī as Agile Cavalry General. [Lǐ] Fēng secretly spoke with Yellow Gate Overseer Sū Shuò, Yǒngníng Bureau Director Yuè Dūn, and Surplus Follower Deputy Director Liú Xián and others stating: "You sirs reside in the interior, have made many violations of the law, the General-in-Chief is strict and stern, and repeatedly spoken about this. Zhāng Dāng can be a warning." [Sū] Shuò and the rest all agreed to follow orders. <a href="#annotation-41" id="source-41">[41]</a> The General-in-Chief slightly heard of this plot, invited [Lǐ] Fēng to a meeting, [Lǐ] Fēng was unaware and went, at once killed him. <a href="#annotation-42" id="source-42">[42]</a> The matter was sent down to the relevant managers, arrested [Xiàhóu] Xuán, [Zhāng] Qī, [Sū] Shuò, [Yuè] Dūn, [Liú] Xián and the rest and sent to the Minister of Justice. <a href="#annotation-43" id="source-43">[43]</a> Minister of Justice Zhōng Yù memorialized: "[Lǐ] Fēng and the rest plotted to coerce the Utmost Honored, usurp authority to execute the most senior minister, Great Rebellion Without Morality, request to discuss it following the law." Thereupon gathered the Excellencies and Ministers and Court councilors and Minister of Justice to discuss, all believed: "[Lǐ] Fēng and the rest each receved exceptional favor, managed and administered the critical and confidential, [Zhāng] Qī held the honor of the in-law relation pepper rooms,^[The pepper rooms (jiāo fáng) referred to the households of the Empress. The name referred to a Hàn dynasty era Palace of that name, referring to the use of a pepper paint for its fragrance.] [Xiàhóu] Xuán served as a generational minister, both residing in ranked positions, but secretly hid disastrous hearts, plotting vicious rebellion, consorting with castrate eunuchs, entrusting them with treasonous plans, in fear of heavenly authority, not daring to openly plot, instead wishing to coerce lord and threaten superior, indulging in their deceit and cruelty, plotting to execute the good assistant, usurp authority to establish one another, about to overturn the capital house, topple and endanger the State Altars. What [Zhōng] Yù has standardized is all in accordance to law, reply to [Zhōng] Yù to put it into effect." Edict said: "The Senior Princess of Qí is the Former Emperor's beloved legacy, pardon her three children from death." Thereupon [Lǐ] Fēng, [Xiàhóu] Xuán, [Zhāng] Qī, [Yuè] Dūn, [Liú] Xián and others were all exterminated three clans, <a href="#annotation-44" id="source-44">[44]</a> the remaining kin and dependents were exiled to Lèlàng prefecture. [Xiàhóu] Xuán in bearing was tolerant and magnanimous, facing execution in the East Market, his expression did not change, his movements were at ease, at the time aged forty-six. <a href="#annotation-45" id="source-45">[45]</a> During Zhèngyuán [254 - 255], to continue the successions of accomplished ministers, enfeoffed [Xiàhóu] Shàng's cousin's grandson [Xiàhóu] Běn as Marquess of Chānglíng precinct, estate three hundred households, to serve as [Xiàhóu] Shàng's posterity.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
頃之，為征西將軍，假節都督雍、涼州諸軍事。〔一〕與曹爽共興駱谷之役，時人譏之。爽誅，徵玄為大鴻臚，數年徙太常。玄以爽抑絀，內不得意。中書令李豐雖宿為大將軍司馬景王所親待，然私心在玄，遂結皇后父光祿大夫張緝，謀欲以玄輔政。豐既內握權柄，子尚公主，又與緝俱馮翊人，故緝信之。豐陰令弟兗州刺史翼求入朝，欲使將兵入，并力起。會翼求朝，不聽。嘉平六年二月，當拜貴人，豐等欲因御臨軒，諸門有陛兵，誅大將軍，以玄代之，以緝為驃騎將軍。豐密語黃門監蘇鑠、永寧署令樂敦、宂從僕射劉賢等曰：「卿諸人居內，多有不法，大將軍嚴毅，累以為言，張當可以為誡。」鑠等皆許以從命。〔二〕大將軍微聞其謀，請豐相見，豐不知而往，即殺之。〔三〕事下有司，收玄、緝、鑠、敦、賢等送廷尉。〔四〕廷尉鍾毓奏：「豐等謀迫脅至尊，擅誅冢宰，大逆無道，請論如法。」於是會公卿朝臣廷尉議，咸以為「豐等各受殊寵，典綜機密，緝承外戚椒房之尊，玄備世臣，並居列位，而包藏禍心，搆圖凶逆，交關閹豎，授以姦計，畏憚天威，不敢顯謀，乃欲要君脅上，肆其詐虐，謀誅良輔，擅相建立，將以傾覆京室，顛危社稷。毓所正皆如科律，報毓施行」。詔書：「齊長公主，先帝遺愛，原其三子死命。」於是豐、玄、緝、敦、賢等皆夷三族，〔五〕其餘親屬徙樂浪郡。玄格量弘濟，臨斬東巿，顏色不變，舉動自若，時年四十六。〔六〕正元中，紹功臣世，封尚從孫本為昌陵亭侯，邑三百戶，以奉尚後。
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-40" id="annotation-40">[40]</a> Wèi lüè states: [Xiàhóu] Xuán had been promoted, Sīmǎ [Shī] Jǐng-wáng succeeded him as Protector of the Army. Protector of the Army presided over the various officers, appointed to manage military office selections and nominations, beginning to end those that had held this office had been unable to stop bribery. Therefore at the time when Jiǎng Jì was Protector of the Army, there was a folk song: "Wishing to seek Ivory Gate, one must have a thousand pǐ; a hundred men supervisor, five hundred pǐ."^[Pǐ is a unit of silk.] [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng and [Jiǎng] Jì were friends, he privately asked [Jiǎng] Jì about it, [Jiǎng] Jì had no way to explain it, and therefore jokingly said: "In Luò's central market purchases, if a single coin is lacking then it is not enacted." Therefore facing one another they laughed. [Xiàhóu] Xuán succeeded [Jiǎng] Jì, and therefore was not able to stop and cut off human affairs. Reaching to [Sīmǎ Shī] Jǐng-wáng succeeding [Xiàhóu] Xuán, he organized laws and decrees, of people none violated.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　魏略曰：玄既遷，司馬景王代為護軍。護軍總統諸將，任主武官選舉，前後當此官者，不能止貨賂。故蔣濟為護軍時，有謠言「欲求牙門，當得千匹；百人督，五百匹」。宣王與濟善，閒以問濟，濟無以解之，因戲曰：「洛中市買，一錢不足則不行。」遂相對歡笑。玄代濟，故不能止絕人事。及景王之代玄，整頓法令，人莫犯者。
:::
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-41" id="annotation-41">[41]</a> Wèi shū states: [Xiàhóu] Xuán had formerly been noble, due to [Cáo] Shuǎng was deposed and dismissed, resided ever in resentment and discontent. Central Writers Director Lǐ Fēng with [Xiàhóu] Xuán and the Empress's father Radiant Grandee Zhāng Qī secretly plotted to make chaos, [Zhāng] Qī with [Lǐ] Fēng were of the same prefecture and was a cunning crafty man, from Dōngguǎn Administrator had been summoned due to being of the Empress' family, also was discontent, and therefore they all together plotted. Previously, [Lǐ] Fēng himself believed he personally occupied the critical and confidential, his son [Lǐ] Tāo also as a Ranked Marquess was Dispensing Affairs Central, bestowed the Senior Princess of Qí, having value inside and outside, his heart could not be at ease. Secretly he spoke with [Lǐ] Tāo stating: "[Xiàhóu] Xuán already is a valued man Within the Seas, and additionally should have great responsibilities, his age is at his prime yet he forever meets with abandonment, and also is Cáo Shuǎng's maternal younger cousin, with the General-in-Chief having enmities. I have obtained [Xiàhóu] Xuán's letters, and deeply worry about this. [Zhāng] Qī has talent and ability, relinquished troops and horses in a large prefecture, returning to sit idly at home. Each do not obtain their ambitions, I wish to send you to inform them of the secret plans." [Zhāng] Qī once was ill and bedridden, [Lǐ] Fēng sent [Lǐ] Tāo to check on his illness, [Lǐ] Tāo dismissed the others and spoke with [Zhāng] Qī stating: "[I, Lǐ] Tāo was bestowed a princess, father and son are in the critical close, the General-in-Chief controls affairs, we always fear to not meet with understanding and trust, the Minister of Ceremonies also feels deep anxiety. Although you Lord Marquess have the honor of being the Empress's father, security and danger cannot yet be known, you have all the same concerns as [my, Lǐ] Tāo's family. [My, Lǐ] Tāo's father wishes to with you Lord Marquess plan about this." [Zhāng] Qī was silent for a long time and said: "In the difficulties of sharing a boat, where can I flee? This is a great affair, to not succeed is for disaster to reach the entire clan." [Lǐ] Tāo thereupon went to report to [Lǐ] Fēng. Secretly speaking with Yellow Gate Overseer Sū Shuò and others, Sū Shuò and the others answered to [Lǐ] Fēng: "We will follow the Lord Marquess's plans." [Lǐ] Fēng spoke stating: "Now in the appointment of a Noble Lady, the various camp troops all garrison the gates. His Majesty will oversee the pavilion, taking advantage of this to then together surround him, we will lead the various offices of men and troops, to then execute the General-in-Chief. You all will together secretly inform him of this intention." [Sū] Shuò and the other said: "If His Majesty perhaps does not follow, what then?" [Lǐ] Fēng said: "Affairs have their expediences. At the time if he does not trust and listen, then merely take him away. How can he not follow?" [Sū] Shuò and the rest agreed. [Lǐ] Fēng said: "This is a matter of clan exterminations, you all keep it confidential. If the matter succeeds, you all will be enfeoffed as Marquesses and Regular Attendants." [Lǐ] Fēng again secretly informed [Xiàhóu] Xuán and [Zhāng] Qī. [Zhāng] Qī sent his son [Zhāng] Miǎo to with [Lǐ] Fēng join with one another and together plot the uprising affairs.

Shìyǔ states: [Lǐ] Fēng sent his son [Lǐ] Tāo to report the plan to [Xiàhóu] Xuán. [Xiàhóu] Xuán said: "It should be considered in detail," but did not report it.
:::

:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔二〕　魏書曰：玄素貴，以爽故廢黜，居常怏怏不得意。中書令李豐與玄及后父光祿大夫張緝陰謀為亂，緝與豐同郡，傾巧人也，以東莞太守召，為后家，亦不得意，故皆同謀。初，豐自以身處機密，息韜又以列侯給事中，尚齊長公主，有內外之重，心不自安。密謂韜曰：「玄既為海內重人，加以當大任，年時方壯而永見廢，又親曹爽外弟，於大將軍有嫌。吾得玄書，深以為憂。緝有才用，棄兵馬大郡，還坐家巷。各不得志，欲使汝以密計告之。」緝嘗病創臥，豐遣韜省病，韜屏人語緝曰：「韜尚公主，父子在機近，大將軍秉事，常恐不見明信，太常亦懷深憂。君侯雖有后父之尊，安危未可知，皆與韜家同慮者也，韜父欲與君侯謀之。」緝默然良久曰：「同舟之難，吾焉所逃？此大事，不捷即禍及宗族。」韜於是往報豐。密語黃門監蘇鑠等，蘇鑠等答豐：「惟君侯計。」豐言曰：「今拜貴人，諸營兵皆屯門。陛下臨軒，因此便共迫脅，將群寮人兵，就誅大將軍。卿等當共密白此意。」鑠等曰；「陛下儻不從人，奈何？」豐等曰：「事有權宜，臨時若不信聽，便當劫將去耳。那得不從？」鑠等許諾。豐曰：「此族滅事，卿等密之。事成，卿等皆當封侯常侍也。」豐復密以告玄、緝。緝遣子邈與豐相結，同謀起事。世語曰：豐遣子韜以謀報玄，玄曰「宜詳之耳」，而不以告也。
:::
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-42" id="annotation-42">[42]</a> Shìyǔ states: The General-in-Chief heard of [Lǐ] Fēng's plot, Resident Wáng Yàng requested for orders to invite [Lǐ] Fēng: "If [Lǐ] Fēng is without preparations, his circumstance constrained and situation pressured, he will certainly come. If he does not come, [I, Wáng] Yàng one man alone am sufficient to restrain him. If he knows the plot has leaked, he will with multitudes clasp wields, long halberds defend himself, directly enter Yúnlóng Gate, seize Heaven's Son and ascend Língyún Terrace. Atop the terrace are three thousand men with weapons, trumpeting and drumming to gather multitudes. If it comes to this, [I, Wáng] Yàng cannot reach him." The General-in-Chief thus sent [Wáng] Yàng with a chariot to invite him. [Lǐ] Fēng was coerced and pressured, accompanied [Wáng] Yàng and arrived.

Wèi-shì Chūnqiū states: The General-in-Chief rebuked [Lǐ] Fēng. [Lǐ] Fēng knew disaster had arrived, and therefore with stern expression said: "You and your father harbor treachery, about to overturn the State Altars. I only regret that my strength is inferior, unable to capture and extermiante you!" The General-in-Chief was furious, and had strong warriors with a saber pommel strike [Lǐ] Fēng's waist, killing him.

Wèi lüè states: [Lǐ] Fēng appellation Ānguó was former Minister of the Guard Lǐ Yì's son. During Huángchū, due to his father's appointment he was summoned to accompany the army. Beginning in the time he was in plain clothes, aged seventeen to eighteen, around Yè he was famed for purity, for understanding and evaluating people, Within the Seas was in agreement, none not taking note of him. Later he accompanied the army and was at Xǔchāng, his acclaim daily expanded. His father did not agree with this, and therefore ordered to shut the gates, commanding to have him cut off from guests. Previously, when Emperor Míng was at the East Palace, [Lǐ] Fēng was among his Literary Scholars. Reaching to succeeding the Honored Throne, he obtained a Wú surrendered man, and asked: "Who are the famed servicemen of the Central States that are heard of east of the Jiāng?" The surrendered man said: "We have heard of a Lǐ Ānguó." At the time [Lǐ] Fēng was a Yellow Gate Cadet, Emperor Míng asked his Left and Right where [Lǐ] Ānguó was, the Left and Right replied with [Lǐ] Fēng. The Emperor said: "Has [Lǐ] Fēng's fame thus spread to Wú and Yuè?" Later transferred to Cavalry Commandant, Dispensing Affairs Central. After the Emperor passed away, became Yǒngníng Minsiter Charioteer. As his fame surpassed the truth, his ability to be employed was little. During Zhèngshǐ [240 - 249], promoted to Attendant Central Secretariat Writers Deputy Director. [Lǐ] Fēng at the Terrace Offices always often claimed illness. At the time Terrace Regulations was that when illness filled a hundred days one would lose salary. When [Lǐ] Fēng's illness had not yet filled several tens of days, at once he would temporarily rise, and then return to bed, and it was like this for several years. Prevoiusly, [Lǐ] Fēng's son [Lǐ] Tāo was selected to be bestowed a princess, [Lǐ] Fēng although outside declined it, inside he was not very apprehensive. [Lǐ] Fēng's younger brothers [Lǐ] Yì and [Lǐ] Wěi served for several years, both successively as prefecture Administrators. [Lǐ] Fēng once among other people prominently admonished his two younger brothers, saying they should use their honored positions for [missing character]. Reaching to when Sīmǎ [Yì] Xuān-wáng was ill for a long time, [Lǐ] Wěi was a Two Thousand dàn, indulged in alcohol, disordering Xīnpíng and Fúfēng two prefectures, but [Lǐ] Fēng did not summon him, everyone believed it relying on favor. When Cáo Shuǎng controlled the government, [Lǐ] Fēng vacillated between the two Excellencies, without having a definite side, therefore at the time there was a slanderous letter that said: "Cáo Shuǎng's power is hot like soup, the Grand Tutor father and sons cold like paste, Lǐ Fēng and his brothers like wandering lights." Its meaning was that although [Lǐ] Fēng outside showed purity and tranquility, yet inside plotted affairs, having similarity to wandering lights.^[Wandering lights (yóu guāng) is a name for a number of different legends and myths. Likely the one referred here is a ghostly light, similar to the will-o'-wisp.] Reaching to when [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng memorialized to execute [Cáo] Shuǎng, he stopped his chariot below the watchtowers, with [Lǐ] Fēng exchanging news, [Lǐ] Fēng was terrified, suddenly his breath stopped, his legs fell limp to the ground, unable to rise. Reaching Jiāpíng Fourth Year after [Sīmǎ Yì] Xuān-wáng had died, the Central Writers Director position was vacant, the General-in-Chief [Sīmǎ Shī] consulted and asked the Court councilors: "Who can fill it?" Someone pointed toward [Lǐ] Fēng. Although [Lǐ] Fēng knew this was not a prestigious selection, yet himself believed he was joined by marriage with the country, thought to attach to the Utmost Honored, and therefore prostrated without declining, therefore memorialized to employ him. [Lǐ] Fēng was the Central Writers for two years, the Emperor almost always alone summoned and spoke with him, it was unknown what was said. [Sīmǎ Shī] Jǐng-wáng knew they were discussing him, invited [Lǐ] Fēng, [Lǐ] Fēng would not report the truth, thus killed him. The affair was kept secret. [Lǐ] Fēng beginning to end served successively Two Courts, did not give attention to household finances, relying on his salary and grain stipend and nothing more. Although [Lǐ] Tāo was bestowed a princess, [Lǐ] Fēng always restricted and warned him to not infringe or take anything. At times obtaining bestowals of cash and silk, at once he outside distributed it to kin and clan. When there were bestowals of Palace women, most gave them to junior relatives, but [Lǐ] Fēng all gave them to his various sister's sons. Reaching to after he died, relevant managers audited his household, the household was without remaining accumulations.

Wèi-shì Chūnqiū states: In the night sent [Lǐ] Fēng's corpse to give over the Minister of Justice. Minister of Justice Zhōng Yù would not accept, stating: "This is not what the law office manages." He was informed of the situation, and moreover commanded to, and so accepted it. The Emperor was angry, about to investigate the circumstances of [Lǐ] Fēng's death. The Dowager Empress was afraid, called the Emperor inside, and so it stopped. Sent envoy to arrest [Lǐ] Yì.

Shìyǔ states: [Lǐ] Yì's later wife was Cavalier Regular Attendant Xún Yì's older sister, spoke to [Lǐ] Yì stating: "The Central Writers affair is discovered, you can when the letters have not yet arrived flee to Wú, why sit and wait for death? Of your Left and Right who can with you together go through water and fire?" [Lǐ] Yì thought and could not answer, his wife said: "You governed a large province, do not know anyone who can with you share in death or life, to flee also is to not escape." [Lǐ] Yì said: "My two sons are small. I will not flee. Now I am only implicated by connection, I will die, but the two sons will certainly be spared." Indeed it was as [Lǐ] Yì said. [Lǐ] Yì's son [Lǐ] Bīn was Yáng Jùn's sister's son. At Jìn Emperor Huì's beginning, he became Hénán Intendant, with [Yáng] Jùn together died, see Jìn shū.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔三〕　世語曰：大將軍聞豐謀，舍人王羕請以命請豐。「豐若無備，情屈勢迫，必來，若不來，羕一人足以制之；若知謀泄，以眾挾輪，長戟自衛，徑入雲龍門，挾天子登淩雲臺，臺上有三千人仗，鳴鼓會眾，如此，羕所不及也」。大將軍乃遣羕以車迎之。豐見劫迫，隨羕而至。魏氏春秋曰：大將軍責豐，豐知禍及，遂正色曰：「卿父子懷姦，將傾社稷，惜吾力劣，不能相禽滅耳！」大將軍怒，使勇士以刀環築豐腰，殺之。魏略曰：豐字安國，故衛尉李義子也。黃初中，以父任召隨軍。始為白衣時，年十七八，在鄴下名為清白，識別人物，海內翕然，莫不注意。後隨軍在許昌，聲稱日隆。其父不願其然，遂令閉門，敕使斷客。初，明帝在東宮，豐在文學中。及即尊位，得吳降人，問「江東聞中國名士為誰」？降人云：「聞有李安國者是。」時豐為黃門郎，明帝問左右安國所在，左右以豐對。帝曰：「豐名乃被于吳越邪？」後轉騎都尉、給事中。帝崩後，為永寧太僕，以名過其實，能用少也。正始中，遷侍中尚書僕射。豐在臺省，常多託疾，時臺制，疾滿百日當解祿，豐疾未滿數十日，輒暫起，已復臥，如是數歲。初，豐子韜以選尚公主，豐雖外辭之，內不甚憚也。豐弟翼及偉，仕數歲間，並歷郡守。豐嘗於人中顯誡二弟，言當用榮位為〔囗〕。及司馬宣王久病，偉為二千石，荒于酒，亂新平、扶風二郡而豐不召，眾人以為恃寵。曹爽專政，豐依違二公間，無有適莫，故于時有謗書曰：「曹爽之勢熱如湯，太傅父子冷如漿，李豐兄弟如游光。」其意以為豐雖外示清淨，而內圖事，有似於游光也。及宣王奏誅爽，住車闕下，與豐相聞，豐怖，遽氣索，足委地不能起。至嘉平四年宣王終後，中書令缺，大將軍諮問朝臣：「誰可補者？」或指向豐。豐雖知此非顯選，而自以連婚國家，思附至尊，因伏不辭，遂奏用之。豐為中書二歲，帝比每獨召與語，不知所說。景王知其議己，請豐，豐不以實告，乃殺之。其事祕。豐前後仕歷二朝，不以家計為意，仰俸廩而已。韜雖尚公主，豐常約敕不得有所侵取，時得賜錢帛，輒以外施親族；及得賜宮人，多與子弟，而豐皆以與諸外甥。及死後，有司籍其家，家無餘積。魏氏春秋曰：夜送豐尸付廷尉，廷尉鍾毓不受，曰：「非法官所治也。」以其狀告，且敕之，乃受。帝怒，將問豐死意，太后懼，呼帝入，乃止。遣使收翼。世語曰：翼後妻，散騎常侍荀廙姊，謂翼曰：「中書事發，可及書未至赴吳，何為坐取死亡！左右可共同赴水火者誰？」翼思未答，妻曰：「君在大州，不知可與同死生者，去亦不免。」翼曰：「二兒小，吾不去。今但從坐，身死，二兒必免。」果如翼言。翼子斌，楊駿外甥也。晉惠帝初，為河南尹，與駿俱死，見晉書。
:::

<a href="#source-43" id="annotation-43">[43]</a> Shìyǔ states: [Xiàhóu] Xuán reached the Minister of Justice, would not agree to submit a statement. Minister of Justice Zhōng Yù personally oversaw the investigation of [Xiàhóu] Xuán. [Xiàhóu] Xuán with stern expression rebuked [Zhōng] Yù stating: "What statement should I make? You are a director-scribe for accusing people, you will make one for me." [Zhōng] Yù believed that him a famed serviceman with integrity high that could not be bent, but the case needed its conclusion, in the night composed a statement, making it adhere with the situation, and shedding tears showed it to [Xiàhóu] Xuán. [Xiàhóu] Xuán looked and nodded at it and nothing more.^[The conviction of Xiàhóu Xuán was already pre-determined. Xiàhóu Xuán refused to participate in the farce and therefore refused to make a statement. Zhōng Yù therefore was obligated to compose a confession for Xiàhóu Xuán, making the confession adhere to the needs of the conviction.] [Zhōng] Yù's younger brother [Zhōng] Huì was younger than [Xiàhóu] Xuán, [Xiàhóu] Xuán had not associated with him. That day he was seated with [Zhōng] Yù and acted overly familiar toward [Xiàhóu] Xuán, [Xiàhóu] Xuán would not accept.

Sūn Shèng's Záyǔ states: [Xiàhóu] Xuán was in prison, [Zhōng] Huì took advantage to wish to be overly familiar with and befriend [Xiàhóu] Xuán. [Xiàhóu] Xuán with stern expression said: "Lord Zhōng why press me like this?"
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔四〕　世語曰：玄至廷尉，不肯下辭。廷尉鍾毓自臨治玄。玄正色責毓曰：「吾當何辭？卿為令史責人也，卿便為吾作。」毓以其名士，節高不可屈，而獄當竟，夜為作辭，令與事相附，流涕以示玄。玄視，頷之而已。毓弟會，年少於玄，玄不與交，是日於毓坐狎玄，玄不受。孫盛雜語曰：玄在囹圄，會因欲狎而友玄，玄正色曰：「鍾君何相偪如此也！」
:::
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-44" id="annotation-44">[44]</a> Wèi shū states: [Lǐ] Fēng's son [Lǐ] Tāo due to being bestowed a princess was bestowed death inside the prison.

::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔五〕　魏書曰：豐子韜，以尚主，賜死獄中。
:::
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-45" id="annotation-45">[45]</a> Wèilüè states: When [Xiàhóu] Xuán from the west returned, he did not interact in social affairs, and did not cultivate flowery ornamentation.

Wèi-shì Chūnqiū states: Previously, Xiàhóu Bà was about to flee to Shǔ, called on [Xiàhóu] Xuán wishing to go with him. [Xiàhóu] Xuán said: "How can I uselessly cling to life by becoming a guest of enemy caitiffs?" Therefore he returned to the capital region. When the Grand Tutor [Sīmǎ Yì] died, Xǔ Yǔn spoke to [Xiàhóu] Xuán stating: "You have no further worries." [Xiàhóu] Xuán sighed and said: "Shìzōng, how can you not see the situation? This man yet was able to deal with me as a younger man of a connected family, [Sīmǎ Shī] Zǐyuán and [Sīmǎ Zhāo] Zǐshàng cannot tolerate me." [Xiàhóu] Xuán once wrote Discourses on Yuè Yì, Zhāng Liáng, and the Original Lack of Mutiliation Punishments, the statements and meanings profound and far-reaching, all transmitted through the world. When [Xiàhóu] Xuán was arrested, Guard General Sīmǎ [Zhāo] Wén-wáng shed tears and pleaded for him, the General-in-Chief [Sīmǎ Shī] said: "Have you forgotten the gathering at Excellency of Works Zhào's burial?" Before this, Excellency of Works Zhào Yǎn had died, the General-in-Chief and his brothers gathered at the burial, the guests numbered in the hundreds. [Xiàhóu] Xuán arrived late, the multitude of guests all rose from their seats to greet him, the General-in-Chief because of this feared him.

Your Servant Sōngzhī notes: Cáo Shuǎng in Zhèngshǐ Fifth Year [244] attacked Shǔ, at the time [Xiàhóu] Xuán already was Overall Supervisor of Guānzhōng, reaching the Tenth Year [249], after [Cáo] Shuǎng was executed and exterminated, only then did he return to Luò. Citing Shào-dì jì, Excellency of Works Zhào Yǎn in the Sixth Year [245] died, [Xiàhóu] Xuán then had no way to attend [Zhào] Yǎn's burial. If it is claimed that [Xiàhóu] Xuán attended Court, the annals and biographies also are without such a situation. This is probably not true.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔六〕　魏略曰：玄自從西還，不交人事，不蓄華妍。魏氏春秋曰：初，夏侯霸將奔蜀，呼玄欲與之俱。玄曰：「吾豈苟存自客於寇虜乎？」遂還京師。太傅薨，許允謂玄曰：「無復憂矣。」玄歎曰：「士宗，卿何不見事乎？此人猶能以通家年少遇我，子元、子上不吾容也。」玄嘗著樂毅、張良及本無肉刑論，辭旨通遠，咸傳于世。玄之執也，衛將軍司馬文王流涕請之，大將軍曰：「卿忘會趙司空葬乎？」先是，司空趙儼薨，大將軍兄弟會葬，賓客以百數，玄時後至，眾賓客咸越席而迎，大將軍由是惡之。臣松之案：曹爽以正始五年伐蜀，時玄已為關中都督，至十年，爽誅滅後，方還洛耳。案少帝紀，司空趙儼以六年亡，玄則無由得會儼葬，若云玄入朝，紀、傳又無其事。斯近妄不實。
:::
:::
:::

#### Xǔ Yǔn {.unnumbered #xuyun}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Previously, Central Manager of the Army Gāoyáng's Xǔ Yǔn with [Lǐ] Fēng and [Xiàhóu] Xuán was close and friendly. Before this there was a forged one-chǐ Edict letter, appointing [Xiàhóu] Xuán as General-in-Chief, [Xǔ] Yǔn as Grand Commandant, together overseeing Secretariat Writers affairs. There was an unknown person before dawn riding a horse with the Edict tablet, handed it to [Xǔ] Yǔn's gate clerk, stating: "There is an Edict," and then galloping away. [Xǔ] Yǔn at once threw the letter into a fire and burned it, not opening and presenting it to Sīmǎ [Shī] Jǐng-wáng. Later when the matter of [Lǐ] Fēng and the rest was discovered, transferred [Xǔ] Yǔn to Defending North General, Lent Stave as Overall Supervisor of Héběi's varous military affairs. Before setting out, for giving out government property, arrested and sent to the Minister of Justice, exiled to Lèlàng, died on the road. <a href="#annotation-46" id="source-46">[46]</a>
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
初，中領軍高陽許允與豐、玄親善。先是有詐作尺一詔書，以玄為大將軍，允為太尉，共錄尚書事。有何人天未明乘馬以詔版付允門吏，曰「有詔」，因便馳走。允即投書燒之，不以開呈司馬景王。後豐等事覺，徙允為鎮北將軍，假節督河北諸軍事。未發，以放散官物，收付廷尉，徙樂浪，道死。〔一〕
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-46" id="annotation-46">[46]</a> Wèilüè states: [Xǔ] Yǔn appellation Shìzōng was of a generationally powerful clan. His father [Xǔ] Jù served successively as Managing Agriculture Colonel and prefecture Administrator. [Xǔ] Yǔn as a youth with his same prefecture's Cuī Zàn both were famed in Jì Province, summoned to enter the army. In Emperor Míng's time became Secretariat Writers Selections Department Cadet, with Chén state's Yuán Kǎn partnered, together implicated in an office affair, both arrested and sent to prison, the Edict's intentions were strict and harsh, certain to have death penalties, with the upright one having heavier punishment. [Xǔ] Yǔn spoke with [Yuán] Kǎn stating: "You are an accomplished minister's son, by law there should be the Eight Deliberations, you do not worry of death." [Yuán] Kǎn understood his intention, and so accepted the heavier punishment. [Xǔ] Yǔn's punishment completed and he was restored as a clerk, sent out as a prefecture Administrator, gradually promoted to Attendant Central Secretariat Writer Central Manager of the Army. [Xǔ] Yǔn heared that Lǐ Fēng and the rest had been arrested, wished to go see the General-in-Chief, had already exited the gates, turned and hesitated undecided, in the middle of the way returned to fetch scallions, [Lǐ] Fēng and the rest were already arrested completely. The General-in-Chief heard of [Xǔ] Yǔn's previous hurry, was bewildered by it and said: "I myself arrested [Lǐ] Fēng and the rest, I don't know why the scholar officials are rushing about." At the time the Court councilors that were rushing were many, but everyone all knew he was thinking of [Xǔ] Yǔn. It happened that Defending North General Liú Jìng died, the Court appointed [Xǔ] Yǔn to succeed [Liú] Jìng. Having already received the Stave and Transfers, he went out to stay in an outer lodge. The General-in-Chief's letter to [Xǔ] Yǔn said: "Although the Defending North has few affairs, yet it supervises and manages an entire region. I think of you beating flowery drums, establishing vermilion staves, through your home province, this is what is called 'Walking in daytime wearing embroidery." [Xǔ] Yǔn in heart was extremely pleased, with the Terrace interior exchanged news, wishing to exchange his drums and trumpets and banners and flags. His elder brother's son [Xǔ] Sù tended to hear of everyone saying that [Xǔ] Yǔn had previously met with suspicion, warned [Xǔ] Yǔn: "You should merely hurry off, what use is this?" [Xǔ] Yǔn said: "You are a common serviceman and do not understand, I am only glorifying the state, and therefore request this." The Emperor because [Xǔ] Yǔn was about to depart thus had Edict to gather the various ministers, the various ministers all gathered, the Emperor specially summoned [Xǔ] Yǔn to come close. [Xǔ] Yǔn formerly had been an Attendant Central, considering he was about to be separated from the Emperor, he shed tears and sobbed. The gathering finished, ended and went out, Edict urged [Xǔ] Yǔn to quickly leave. It happened that relevant managers memorialized that [Xǔ] Yǔn had formerly without authority had kitchen cash and grain given to various performers and his office associates, therefore then arrested and sent to the Minister of Justice, the investigation and interrogation completed, spared death by exile to the borders. [Xǔ] Yǔn in Jiāpíng Sixth Year Autumn was exiled, his wife and children not permitted to accompany him, on the road and not yet arrived, in that year's winter he died.

Wèi-shì Chūnqiū states: [Xǔ] Yǔn became a Personnel Department Cadet, selecting prefecture Administrator. Emperor Míng suspected the employments were not in order, summoned him to enter, about to apply punishments. [Xǔ] Yǔn's wife Ruǎn-shì barefooted went out, speaking stating: "An enlightened ruler can be persuaded by logic, difficult to be appealed by emotion." [Xǔ] Yǔn nodded to her and then entered. The Emperor angrily interrogated him, [Xǔ] Yǔn replied stating: "Although this prefecture's Administrator's term limit document letter first arrived, the age limit was later. Although this other Administrator was later, the day limit was before." The Emperor took the matters in front and looked at them, and then released and sent him out. Looking out and seeing his clothing was damaged, he said: "This is a pure clerk." Bestowed on him. When [Xǔ] Yǔn was sent out as Defending North, he happily spoke with his wife stating: "I know I have escaped." The wife said: "Disaster is seen in this, what escape is there?" [Xǔ] Yǔn excelled in appraising seals, when about to be appointed, because the seal was not good, he had it again recarved. It was like this three times. [Xǔ] Yǔn said: "Although the seal is just completed yet it is already disgraced." Asked the seal deliverer, and indeed in carrying it had fallen in a lavatory.

Xiāng Yìn shū states: "The method of appraising seals originally came from Chén [Qún] Chángwén. Chángwén spoke of it to Wéi Zhòngjiāng, seal crafter Yáng Lì from Zhòngjiāng received the method, spoke of it to Xǔ Shìzōng. [Yáng] Lì with the method divined good and bad fortune, out of ten able to be correct nine to eight. Zhòngjiāng asked Chángwén 'How did you obtain the method from?' Chángwén said: 'It originally came from the Hàn era. There were classics on appraising seals, appraising tablets, also there were classics on hawks, classics on oxen, classics on horses. Seal crafter Zōng Yǎng spoke of the method to Chéng Shēnbó, therefore there were twelve schools of appraisal methods transmitted to the world.'"

[Xǔ] Yǔn's wife Ruǎn-shì was worthy and enlightened but ugly, [Xǔ] Yǔn on first seeing her was amazed, after the marriage rituals finished, he had no intention to enter (her room) again. The wife sent a maidservant to spy on him, saying: "There is a guest surnamed Huán." The wife said: "It must be Huán Fàn, he will urge him to enter." Soon after [Huán] Fàn indeed urged him, [Xǔ] Yǔn entered, and immediately then rose, the wife clutched his garment to detain him. [Xǔ] Yǔn looked back and spoke to the wife stating: "Women have Four Virtues, how many do you have?" The wife said: "Your new wife lacks only appearance. Servicemen have a Hundred Conducts, how many do you have?" Xǔ said: "All of them." The wife said: "Servicemen have a Hundred Conducts, taking virtue as foremost. You love beauty and do not love virtue, how can you say all of them?" [Xǔ] Yǔn had a shamed expression, knew she was out of the ordinary, and therefore they became close and respected one another. Begat two sons, [Xǔ] Qí and [Xǔ] Měng, from youth had good reputation. [Xǔ] Yǔn later was executed by [Sīmǎ Shī] Jǐng-wáng, his disciple ran to enter to inform his wife, the wife just was at her loom, her expression did not change, and said: "I already knew it would be like this." The disciple wished to hide the children, the wife said: "Do not pre-empt the affairs of the boys." Later they moved to where the grave was, [Sīmǎ Shī] Jǐng-wáng sent Zhōng Huì to watch them, and if their talents and skills and virtues and abilities reached their father's, then arrest them. The boys spoke of this to their mother, their mother answered: "Although you are fine, your talents and capabilities are not many, speak with [Zhōng] Huì from the heart, then you will assuredly be without worries. Do not show utmost grief, when [Zhōng] Huì stops then you stop. Also you can somewhat ask about Court affairs." The boys followed this. [Zhōng] Huì returned from the mission, reported the situation, in the end they escaped from disaster, all by their mother's instructions. Even with [Zhōng] Huì's knowledge and discernment, yet he was beaten by the wisdom of a worthy wife; indeed celebrations reached to later successors, bequeathing fiefs to descendants and nothing more.

Shìyǔ states: [Xǔn] Yǔn's two sons, [Xǔ] Qí appellation Zǐtài, [Xǔ] Měng appellation Zǐbào, both had administration talent and scholarship. During Jìn's Yuánkāng [291 - 299], [Xǔ] Qí was Director of Retainers Colonel, [Xǔ] Měng was Yōu Province Inspector.

Fù Chàng's Jìn Zhūgōng zàn states: [Xǔ] Měng in ritual and music was scholarly and refined, at the time the most exceptional. [Xǔ] Qí's son [Xǔ] Xiá appellation Sīzǔ, for purity and esteem was acclaimed, position reached Attendant Central. [Xǔ] Měng's son [Xǔ] Shì appellation Yízǔ, had talent and competence, reached Púyáng Inner Scribe, Píngyuán Administrator.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　魏略曰：允字士宗，世冠族。父據，仕歷典農校尉、郡守。允少與同郡崔贊俱發名於冀州，召入軍。明帝時為尚書選曹郎，與陳國袁侃對，同坐職事，皆收送獄，詔旨嚴切，當有死者，正直者為重。允謂侃曰：「卿，功臣之子，法應八議，不憂死也。」侃知其指，乃為受重。允刑竟復吏，出為郡守，稍遷為侍中尚書中領軍。允聞李豐等被收，欲往見大將軍，已出門，回遑不定，中道還取蔥，豐等已收訖。大將軍聞允前遽，怪之曰：「我自收豐等，不知士大夫何為匆匆乎？」是時朝臣遽者多耳，而眾人咸以為意在允也。會鎮北將軍劉靜卒，朝廷以允代靜。已受節傳，出止外舍。大將軍與允書曰：「鎮北雖少事，而都典一方，念足下震華鼓，建朱節，歷本州，此所謂著繡晝行也。」允心甚悅，與臺中相聞，欲易其鼓吹旌旗。其兄子素頗聞眾人說允前見嫌意，戒允「但當趣耳，用是為邪」！允曰：「卿俗士不解，我以榮國耳，故求之。」帝以允當出，乃詔會群臣，群臣皆集，帝特引允以自近；允前為侍中，顧當與帝別，涕泣歔欷。會訖，罷出，詔促允令去。會有司奏允前擅以廚錢穀乞諸俳及其官屬，故遂收送廷尉，考問竟，（故）減死徙邊。允以嘉平六年秋徙，妻子不得自隨，行道未到，以其年冬死。魏氏春秋曰：允為吏部郎，選郡守。明帝疑其所用非次，召入，將加罪。允妻阮氏跣出，謂曰：「明主可以理奪，難以情求。」允頷之而入。帝怒詰之，允對曰：「某郡太守雖限滿文書先至，年限在後，〔某守雖後〕，日限在前。」帝前取事視之，乃釋遣出。望其衣敗，曰：「清吏也。」賜之。允之出為鎮北也，喜謂其妻曰：「吾知免矣！」妻曰：「禍見於此，何免之有？」允善相印，將拜，以印不善，使更刻之，如此者三。允曰：「印雖始成而已被辱。」問送印者，果懷之而墜于廁。相印書曰：「相印法本出陳長文，長文以語韋仲將，印工楊利從仲將受法，以語許士宗。利以法術占吉凶，十可中八九。仲將問長文『從誰得法』？長文曰：『本出漢世，有相印、相笏經，又有鷹經、牛經、馬經。印工宗養以法語程申伯，是故有一十二家相法傳于世。』」允妻阮氏賢明而醜，允始見愕然，交禮畢，無復入意。妻遣婢覘之，云「有客姓桓」，妻曰：「是必桓範，將勸使入也。」既而範果勸之。允入，須臾便起，妻捉裾留之。允顧謂婦曰：「婦有四德，卿有其幾？」婦曰：「新婦所乏唯容。士有百行，君有其幾？」許曰：「皆備。」婦曰：「士有百行，以德為首，君好色不好德，何謂皆備？」允有慚色，知其非凡，遂雅相親重。生二子，奇、猛，少有令聞。允後為景王所誅，門生走入告其婦，婦正在機，神色不變，曰：「早知爾耳。」門生欲藏其子，婦曰：「無預諸兒事。」後移居墓所，景王遣鍾會看之，若才藝德能及父，當收。兒以語母，母答：「汝等雖佳，才具不多，率胸懷與會語，便自無憂，不須極哀，會止便止。又可多少問朝事。」兒從之。會反命，具以狀對，卒免其禍，皆母之教也。雖會之識鑒，而輸賢婦之智也。果慶及後嗣，追封子孫而已。世語曰：允二子：奇字子泰，猛字子豹，並有治理才學。晉元康中，奇為司隸校尉，猛幽州刺史。傅暢晉諸公贊曰：猛禮樂儒雅，當時最優。奇子遐，字思祖，以清尚稱，位至侍中。猛子式，字儀祖，有才幹，至濮陽內史、平原太守。
:::

:::

#### Wáng Jīng {.unnumbered #wangjing}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Qīnghé's Wáng Jīng also with [Xǔ] Yǔn both were acclaimed as Jì Province's famed servicemen. During Gānlù [256 - 260] he became a Secretariat Writer, in connection to the Duke of Gāoguì village incident was executed. At first when [Wáng] Jīng became a prefecture Administrator, [Wáng] Jīng's mother spoke to [Wáng] Jīng stating: "You are a farming family's son, now your service reaches the two thousand dàn. Things going too far is inauspicious, you can stop." [Wáng] Jīng did not follow this, successively was Inspector in two provinces, Director of Retainers Colonel, in the end bringing about destruction. <a href="#annotation-47" id="source-47">[47]</a> [Xǔ] Yǔn's friend of the same prefecture Cuī Zàn, also had once warned [Xǔ] Yǔn of flourishing too much in the world. <a href="#annotation-48" id="source-48">[48]</a>
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
清河王經亦與允俱稱冀州名士。甘露中為尚書，坐高貴鄉公事誅。始經為郡守，經母謂經曰：「汝田家子，今仕至二千石，物太過不祥，可以止矣。」經不能從，歷二州刺史，司隸校尉，終以致敗〔一〕。允友人同郡崔贊，亦嘗以處世太盛戒允云。〔二〕
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-47" id="annotation-47">[47]</a> Shìyǔ states: [Wáng] Jīng appellation Yànwěi, previously was Jiāngxià Administrator. General-in-Chief Cáo Shuǎng sent silk fabric of twenty pǐ to trade with Wú, [Wáng] Jīng did not send the letter, abandoned office and returned home. His mother asked the circumstances of his return, [Wáng] Jīng replied with the truth. His mother believed [Wáng] Jīng managed troops and horses but without authority left, and in answer had the escort clerks cane [Wáng] Jīng fifty strokes, [Cáo] Shuǎng heard and did not further punish him. [Wáng] Jīng became Director of Retainers Colonel, recruited Hénèi's Xiàng Xióng as Overall Office Following Official. When Wáng Yè went out, he did not explain [Wáng] Jīng's intentions, so that it reached trouble. When [Wáng] Jīng was executed in the East Market, [Xiàng] Xióng wept for him, emotionally moving the entire market. The execution reached to [Wáng] Jīng's mother, Yōng Province former clerk Huángfǔ Yàn with his family wealth collected and buried her.

Hàn Jìn Chūnqiū states: When [Wáng] Jīng was arrested, he took leave of his mother. His mother's expression did not change, laughed and answered stating: "Of people who does not die? Formerly the reason that I did not stop you was that I feared you would not find your place. To like this share fate, what regret is to be had?" Jìn Emperor Wǔ's Tàishǐ Inaugural Year [265] Edict stated: "Former Secretariat Writer Wáng Jīng, although personally entrapped in penal law, however his maintaining of will can be praised. The household is fallen and lost, my thoughts always pity this, thus bestow on [Wáng] Jīng's grandson Cadet Central position."
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　世語曰：經字（彥偉）〔彥緯〕，初為江夏太守。大將軍曹爽附絹二十匹令交市于吳，經不發書，棄官歸。母問歸狀，經以實對。母以經典兵馬而擅去，對送吏杖經五十，爽聞，不復罪。經為司隸校尉，辟河內向雄為都官從事，王業之出，不申經（竟）〔意〕以及難。經刑於東市，雄哭之，感動一市。刑及經母，雍州故吏皇甫晏以家財收葬焉。漢晉春秋曰：經被收，辭母。母顏色不變，笑而應曰：「人誰不死？往所以不止汝者，恐不得其所也。以此并命，何恨之有哉？」晉武帝太始元年詔曰：「故尚書王經，雖身陷法辟，然守志可嘉。門戶堙沒，意常愍之，其賜經孫郎中。」
:::
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-48" id="annotation-48">[48]</a> Xún Chuò's Jìzhōu jì states: [Cuī] Zàn's son [Cuī] Hóng appellation Liángbó, was pure and scrupulous and had determination to act not for himself, became a Jìn Personnel Department Secretariat Writer, Minister of Agriculture.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}

〔二〕　荀綽冀州記曰：贊子洪，字良伯，清恪有匪躬之志，為晉吏部尚書、大司農。

## Appraisal {.unnumbered}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Appraisal states: The Xiàhóu and Cáo clans for generations intermarried, therefore [Xiàhóu] Dūn, [Xiàhóu] Yuān, [Cáo] Rén, [Cáo] Hóng, [Cáo] Xiū, [Xiàhóu] Shàng, [Cáo] Zhēn and others all as kin and old relations of lungs and guts, were noble and valued at the time, Left and Right of the achievements and enterprise, all having effective labors. [Cáo] Shuǎng's virtue was meager but position honored, submerging into overflowing, this assuredly is what the Dà Yì wrote of, what the Dào school dreaded. [Xiàhóu] Xuán for his standards and bearing, the world praised his name, however he and Cáo Shuǎng inside and outside were inseparably entangled, with glorious position like this, one never hears of rectifying or correcting in (Cáo Shuǎng's) wrongs, or assisting in delivering good talents. Raising this for discussion, how could he have escaped this?
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
評曰：夏侯、曹氏，世為婚姻，故惇、淵、仁、洪、休、尚、真等並以親舊肺腑，貴重于時，左右勳業，咸有效勞。爽德薄位尊，沈溺盈溢，此固大易所著，道家所忌也。玄以規格局度，世稱其名，然與曹爽中外繾綣；榮位如斯，曾未聞匡弼其非，援致良才。舉茲以論，焉能免之乎！
:::
:::
